title: Human Whole Blood PBMC Isolation
author: Nicholas C Buitrago-Pocasangre
materials: Gently invert 50 mL tubes to mix.
Replace volume of removed plasma with equal volume of DPBS, no calcium, no magnesium Thermo Fisher Scientific Catalog #14190144 .

steps.title: Collect Human Blood
steps.instruction: Collect ten blood samples in K2EDTA Vacutainer Tubes (Becton Dickinson (BD) Catalog #366643) from human subjects.

steps.title: Separate Plasma from Whole Blood
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the blood at 500 x g for 10 minutes to separate plasma from whole blood.

steps.title: Prepare Blood for Density Gradient
steps.instruction: Prepare a 1:1 DPBS/Blood mixture in 50 mL conical tubes.

substeps.instruction: Pour or pipet blood into 50 mL conical tubes, ensuring relatively equal volumes and not exceeding 20 mL of whole blood per tube.
Rinse blood tubes with 5 mL DPBS per 2 tubes using a 10 mL serological pipette and add the mixture to the collection tube.
Fill the 50 mL tube with PBS to twice the initial volume of the whole blood to achieve the 1:1 ratio.

steps.title: Layer Lymphoprep
steps.instruction: Carefully layer Lymphoprep (STEMCELL Technologies Inc. Catalog #18060) onto the blood mixture.

substeps.instruction: Aspirate 12.5 mL of Lymphoprep using a 10 mL serological pipet.
Gently place the pipet into the bottom of the 50 mL conical tube and remove the pipet aid to allow the liquid to drain slowly, forming a Ficoll layer at the bottom.
Lift the pipette up and stop at the interface; wait 3 seconds for the last 1 mL of Ficoll to release.
Cap the pipette with your fingers and lift the pipette entirely out of the tube.

steps.title: Isolate PBMC Layer
steps.instruction: Centrifuge the tubes to separate the PBMC layer and transfer the cells.

substeps.instruction: Centrifuge at 800 x g for 20 minutes (acceleration at 4, deceleration at 4) at room temperature.
After 30 minutes, transfer the PBMC layer to a new 50 mL collection tube, ensuring the red blood cell pellet is not touched.

To maximize recovery, remove as much of the PBMC layer as possible on a first pass across all tubes, then repeat with a second pass. (Tip: stabilize the hand by touching the pipette end to the tube wall and tip to the front of the tube).
Uncap the finger from the pipette and transfer the liquid into liquid waste.

steps.title: Wash PBMCs
steps.instruction: Wash the isolated PBMCs using DPBS.

substeps.instruction: Create a 1:1 PBMC layer/DPBS mixture by filling the 50 mL conical tube to twice the volume of the PBMC layer; cap and invert to mix.
Pour off the supernatant with one quick motion.
Resuspend the pellet with 10 mL PBS (the same 10 mL can be used to resuspend and wash up to 4 tubes).
Repeat the rinse with another 10 mL DPBS.
Fill the resuspended pellet up to 50 mL with DPBS and invert the tube to mix.

steps.title: Cell Counting and Final Wash
steps.instruction: Perform a final centrifugation and estimate cell count.

substeps.instruction: Aliquot 10 µL of the resuspension for counting.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 5 minutes (max acceleration: 9, max deceleration: 9) at room temperature.
During the spin, count cells or estimate total PBMCs (expected range: 1-2 million PBMCs/mL of whole blood).

steps.title: Cryopreserve PBMCs
steps.instruction: Resuspend the pellet in freezing media and freeze.

substeps.instruction: Pour off the supernatant.
Resuspend the pellet in Bambanker Cell Freezing Media (Bulldog Bio Catalog #BB05) at a concentration of 10-20e6 cells/1 mL and mix.
Quickly transfer aliquots to a room temperature Mr. Frosty with IPA and transfer to -80 °C.
Centrifuge at 400 x g for 8 minutes (max acceleration: 9, max deceleration: 9) at room temperature.
Remove 5 mL of plasma, mix by inversion or pipet, and aliquot into 1 mL portions.
